review_scope: External drift supplement, not an artifact of the original locked tree

observations.statement: The source describes desktop interaction across supported Copilot CLI/app surfaces on macOS and Windows; this is a capability description, not a mandate to enable it.
Illustrative GUI tasks are examples; structured API, MCP, terminal, filesystem or browser tools are generally more predictable when available.
The enabled agent can inspect accessible or visual content and perform input/navigation; session activity is reviewable.
Desktop computer-use tools require explicit enablement and are disabled initially.
Surface permission settings determine application-control approval; application access can be session-limited, saved or denied.
Saved application permission is local and shared between app and CLI on that computer.
Removing saved approval affects future sessions but does not withdraw access already granted to a running session.
Explicit tool denial overrides saved or automatic approval.
Local enablement cannot override enterprise managed policy disabling computer use.
Active operations can be interrupted using the source-described CLI or app stop controls; no stop behavior was exercised in this review.
macOS accessibility and screen-recording permissions serve distinct control and visual-inspection purposes.
UI variability and unexpected content can cause incorrect or repeated actions; review target, permissions and results for consequential modifications.
Visible application content can include sensitive third-party information; choose tasks and applications consistent with context-sharing consent.
Avoid persistent application approval where sensitive information or high-impact actions make later unprompted control risky.

dependency_observations.statement: The referenced preview fragment declares preview status and changeability, with release phase supplied through a product variable.
